frontmatter.description: A pasted diff with a request that belongs to git-workflow-and-versioning. Guards the "even when the diff is pasted inline" clause of the review skill's description, since a pasted diff alone must not make the review skill fire.
frontmatter.expected_outcome: A commit message; code-review-and-quality is never invoked.

frontmatter.description: A test-first request that belongs to test-driven-development. The review skill must not fire.
frontmatter.expected_outcome: The reply proposes a failing test first; code-review-and-quality is never invoked.

frontmatter.description: A failing-test diagnosis with the diff pasted inline. Checks that debugging-and-error-recovery activates and that the reply names the cause, makes the minimal fix and says how to confirm it.
frontmatter.expected_outcome: The exclusive slice end named as the cause, the one-token fix to start + size, and a way to confirm it, such as re-running the failing test or adding a test that asserts a full page and the last page's boundary.

frontmatter.description: The same pasted diff as the debugging case, requested as a code review without a reported failure. Guards against routing every pasted diff to debugging-and-error-recovery.
frontmatter.expected_outcome: A code review identifying the pagination defect; debugging-and-error-recovery is never invoked.

frontmatter.description: A commit-message request with the diff pasted inline. The diff carries two unrelated changes. The skill should fire, and the reply should give a typed subject with a body that says why, and say that the two concerns belong in separate commits.
frontmatter.expected_outcome: A conventional message for the retry change with a body explaining the transient-failure motivation, and a note that the formatMoney helper is a separate concern deserving its own commit and message; git-workflow-and-versioning is invoked.

frontmatter.description: A pasted diff with a "what broke?" question that belongs to debugging-and-error-recovery. Guards the "even when the diff is pasted inline" clause of the git-workflow-and-versioning description, since a diff on its own must not make the git skill fire.
frontmatter.expected_outcome: A diagnosis of the off-by-one; git-workflow-and-versioning is never invoked.

frontmatter.description: A simplification request with the function pasted inline and nothing else to read. The skill should fire, and the reply should keep every behavior of the original and say what it removed and why that is safe.
frontmatter.expected_outcome: A shorter normalizeTags that still returns [] for null or undefined, splits a string on commas, keeps non-string items such as 0, drops blanks and dedups in first-occurrence order, with the removals explained; code-simplification is invoked.

frontmatter.description: A pasted function with a speed complaint that belongs to performance-optimization. Guards the "even when the code is pasted inline" clause of the code-simplification description, since a request to make pasted code faster must not make the simplification skill fire.
frontmatter.expected_outcome: A faster lookup (a Set or a Map instead of a linear scan per row); code-simplification is never invoked.

frontmatter.name: security-and-hardening
frontmatter.description: Hardens code against vulnerabilities. Use when auditing an input handler for vulnerabilities, when handling user input, authentication, data storage, or external integrations, or when checking a login flow is safe against the OWASP Top Ten. Use when building any feature that accepts untrusted data, manages user sessions or session cookies, or interacts with third-party services. Use when auditing dependencies for known vulnerabilities, triaging package-manager audit findings, or assessing supply-chain risk
A bug fix request with the function pasted inline and no mention of tests. The skill should fire, and the reply should reproduce the bug with a failing test before fixing it.
frontmatter.expected_outcome: A test that reproduces the lost cent, shown or described as failing first, then the fix; test-driven-development is invoked.

frontmatter.description: A pasted diff with a "what broke" question that belongs to debugging-and-error-recovery. Guards the "fix a bug in it" clause of the test-driven-development description, since a bug mentioned in a diagnosis request must not make the TDD skill fire.
frontmatter.expected_outcome: A diagnosis of the off-by-one; test-driven-development is never invoked.

frontmatter.description: A refactor request for readability with the function pasted inline and no behavior change asked for. It belongs to code-simplification. Guards the test-driven-development clause, whose "change its behavior" and "the fix looks too obvious to need a test" must not pull in a request that changes no behavior.
frontmatter.expected_outcome: A clearer version of the function with the same behavior; test-driven-development is never invoked.

frontmatter.name: code-simplification
frontmatter.description: Simplifies code for clarity. Use when refactoring code for clarity without changing behavior. Use when code works but is harder to read, maintain, or extend than it should be. Use when reviewing code that has accumulated unnecessary complexity. Use when asked to simplify, clean up, or reduce the nesting of a function or module that already works, even when the code is pasted inline and nothing else needs to change.

frontmatter.name: debugging-and-error-recovery
frontmatter.description: Guides systematic root-cause debugging. Use when tests fail, builds break, something that worked yesterday broke, behavior doesn't match expectations, or you encounter any unexpected error. Use when you need to figure out what broke and why — a systematic approach to finding and fixing the root cause rather than guessing. Use when asked what broke, why a test started failing, or why code throws, even when the diff, the function, or the stack trace is pasted inline and the cause looks obvious from readi

frontmatter.name: code-review-and-quality
frontmatter.description: Conducts multi-axis code review. Use before merging any change. Use when reviewing code written by yourself, another agent, or a human. Use when you need to assess code quality across multiple dimensions before it enters the main branch. Use when asked to review a diff or a pull request, even when the diff is pasted inline and the review looks quick to do from reading it.

frontmatter.name: test-driven-development
frontmatter.description: Drives development with tests using the red-green-refactor loop. Use when implementing any logic, fixing any bug, or changing any behavior. Use when you need to prove that code works, when a bug report arrives, or when you're about to modify existing functionality. Use when asked to add tests to a function, fix a bug in it or change its behavior, even when the code is pasted inline, the request does not mention tests and the answer looks obvious from reading it. The skill writes the failing test first
